Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:10:1.hebrew: בכלאים - דתרי מיני הוא, פרקינן, דקתני במתניתין: ר"א מתיר בכלאים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:10:1.english: With a hybrid - [Even though] it is of two species, we redeem [with it], as it is taught in the Mishnah: Rabbi Eliezer permits [redeeming] with a hybrid.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:12:1.english: A cow that gave birth to a goat of sorts, one may not redeem - For it is a calf.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:12:2.hebrew: בכלאים פרקינן - וכ"ש בנדמה, ול"ל למיתנייה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:12:2.english: One may redeem with a hybrid - And all the more so with [an animal that merely] resembles [another species]; and why would [the baraita] need to teach it?

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:13:1.english: It itself was needed by him - And it did not come on account of an inference.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:14:1.english: Is it a hybrid? - [This is said] in astonishment: Behold, it is [merely] an animal that resembles [another species]!

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:15:1.english: To what - Is it saying that the Rabbis equated [an animal that] resembles [another species] to a hybrid?

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:15:2.hebrew: אי לקדשים - שלא יקרב לגבי מזבח, ל"ל למתלייה לנדמה בכלאים? כי היכי דפשיטא לן בכלאים, פשיטא לן בנדמה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:15:2.english: If to sacrificial [animals] - That it may not be offered upon the altar — why do I need [the Tanna] to make [an animal that] resembles dependent upon a hybrid? Just as it is obvious to us regarding a hybrid, it is obvious to us regarding [an animal that] resembles.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:16:1.hebrew: אי לבכורה - לאשמועי' דלא קדוש בבכורה ככלאים — פשיטא! ד"אך בכור שור" כתיב, ובהדיא אימעוט:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:16:1.english: If for [the status of] a firstborn - [If it comes] to teach us that it is not sanctified with firstborn status like a hybrid — [this is] obvious! For it is written: “But the firstborn of an ox,” and it is explicitly excluded.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:17:1.hebrew: אי למעט ממעשר - דכי היכי דכלאים לא מעשרין, אף נדמה לא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:17:1.english: If to exclude [it] from tithe - That just as one does not tithe a hybrid, so too [one does] not [tithe] an animal that resembles [another species]:

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:17:2.hebrew: פשיטא! תרווייהו מחד קרא נפקי — "תחת" "תחת": כתיב הכא "תחת השבט", וכתיב בקדשים "תחת אמו". מה התם נדמה וכלאים לא, כדממעטינן לעיל — אף מעשר, כלאים ונדמה לא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:17:2.english: [It is] obvious! Both of them are derived from a single verse — “under” [and] “under”: It is written here, “under the rod” (Leviticus 27:32), and it is written regarding sacrificial animals, “under its mother” (Leviticus 22:27). Just as there, an animal that resembles [another species] and a hybrid are not [fit for sacrifice], as we excluded above, so too [regarding] animal tithe, a hybrid and an animal that resembles [another species] are not [fit].

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:17:3.hebrew: לפטר חמור - דלא פרקינן ביה פטר חמור, כי כלאים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:17:3.english: To a firstborn donkey - That we do not redeem a firstborn donkey with it, just like [with] a hybrid.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:18:2.hebrew: העברה העברה - כתיב הכא: "יעבור תחת השבט", וכתיב בבכור: "והעברת פטר רחם". מה בבכורה חייב, כדאמרן: "ואם יש בו מקצת סימנין חייב" — אף מעשר נמי ליהוי חייב:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:18:2.english: Passing, passing - It is written here: “shall pass under the rod” (Leviticus 27:32), and it is written regarding a firstborn: “and you shall set apart [literally: cause to pass] all that openeth the womb” (Exodus 13:12). Just as with regard to a firstborn it is obligated, as we have stated: “and if it has some of [the mother’s] characteristics, it is obligated” — so too regarding [animal] tithe, let it also be obligated.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:19:1.hebrew: קמ״ל - דדין כלאים אית ליה, דתחת תחת גמר מקדשים. כי היכי דלמזבח לא קרב — כדאמר בריש פירקין (בכורות דף ג:): "מום קבוע הוא לישחט עליו" — במעשר נמי לא קדוש:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:19:1.english: [The tanna] teaches us - That it has the legal status of a crossbreed [kilayim], for it derives [its rule via the verbal analogy between] “under” [and] “under” from sacrificial animals. Just as it is not offered upon the altar — as [the Gemara] stated at the beginning of our chapter (Bekhorot 3b): “it is a permanent blemish [upon which] to slaughter it” — with regard to [animal] tithe as well, it does not become consecrated.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:1:1.english: Nor with an undomesticated animal - [Such as] a gazelle and a deer.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:1:2.english: Nor with a slaughtered [animal] - And even a slaughtered lamb.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:1:3.english: A tereifa - [Such as an animal] whose legs were severed from the knee joint and above:

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:1:4.english: A hybrid - [The offspring of] a he-goat that mated with a ewe.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:1:5.english: A koy - [It is] uncertain [whether it is] a wild animal [or] uncertain [whether it is] a domesticated animal.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:1:6.english: Because it is a lamb - For both a sheep and a goat are called a lamb.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:1:7.english: [If] he gave it to a priest - The firstborn donkey.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:20:1.english: Disqualified consecrated animals - That were redeemed and go out to unconsecrated status.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:21:1.hebrew: כיון דאמר - פטר חמור מותר בהנאה קודם פדיון, חולין הוא הפטר חמור, ויכול לפדותו בה, דליכא למימר: איסור חל על איסור:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:21:1.english: Since he says - [That] a firstborn donkey is permitted to derive benefit [from it] prior to redemption, the firstborn donkey is non-sacred, and he can redeem it with [a disqualified consecrated animal], for it cannot be said [that] a prohibition takes effect upon a prohibition.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:22:1.hebrew: אין איסור - פטר חמור חל על איסור דבהמת פסולי המוקדשין, אית בה קדושה אפי' לאחר פדיון, דאסירי בגיזה ועבודה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:22:1.english: A prohibition does not - [The prohibition of] a firstborn donkey [does not] take effect upon the prohibition of an animal of disqualified consecrated items; [for] it has sanctity even after redemption, as they are forbidden in shearing and labor.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:23:1.english: That its redemption does not take hold - For the lamb given in its stead has no sanctity in it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:24:1.hebrew: צבי ואיל - כתיב בפסולי המוקדשין, דכתיב (דברים י״ב:ט״ו): "רק בכל אות נפשך וגו'", ובפסולי המוקדשין מדבר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:24:1.english: Gazelle and hart - It is written with regard to disqualified consecrated animals, as it is written (Deuteronomy 12:15): “However, according to all the desire of your soul, etc.,” and it speaks of disqualified consecrated animals.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:2:2.hebrew: לכל השמות - שבמשנתנו. הפסח אינו בא עגל וחיה, דכתיב (שמות יב) שה מן הכבשים ומן העזים; ולא שחוט, דבעינן שחיטה לשם פסח; וכלאים נמי לא, דכלאים אין קריבין לגבי מזבח, כדקתני לקמן: שור וכשב — פרט לכלאים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:2:2.english: All of these names - [Those] that are in our Mishnah. The Paschal offering does not come [from] a calf or an undomesticated animal, as it is written (Exodus 12:5): "A lamb... from the sheep or from the goats"; nor [from an already] slaughtered [animal], as we require slaughter [specifically] for the sake of the Paschal offering; and a hybrid also [may] not [be brought], as hybrids are not offered upon the altar, as it teaches below: "An ox or a sheep" — to exclude a hybrid.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:5:1.hebrew: בן פקועה - שנמצא חי בבהמה שחוטה. פלוגתא דר"מ ורבנן בפ' בהמה המקשה (חולין דף עד.):
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:5:1.english: A ben pekua - [An animal] that was found alive inside a slaughtered animal. The dispute between Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis [is] in the chapter [entitled] Behemah Hamakasheh (Chullin 74a).

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:6:1.hebrew: בדיקולא - קלחת. כלומר: כשחוטה דמי, ואין פודין בשחוטה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:6:1.english: In a pot - A cauldron. That is to say, it is considered like a slaughtered [animal], and one does not redeem with a slaughtered [animal].

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:6:2.hebrew: או דלמא כו' - וכל הנך "אין פודין" דאמר במתניתין, שלא בשויין קאמרינן — דאי בשויין, אפי' בשלקי שרי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:6:2.english: Or perhaps, etc. - And all these [cases of] “one may not redeem” that it stated in the Mishnah, we say [this only when redeeming] not according to their value; for if [redeemed] according to their value, even with boiled vegetables it is permitted.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:8:1.hebrew: בן פקועה פסול לפסח - דאינו קרב למזבח, דתניא בפ' שני דשחיטת חולין (דף לח:): "כי יולד" — פרט ליוצא דופן:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:8:1.english: A ben pekua is unfit for the Paschal offering - For it is not offered upon the altar, as it is taught in the second chapter of [Tractate] Shechitat Chullin (38b): “When it is born” — [this] excludes [an animal born via] Caesarean section.

Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:9:1.hebrew: שה מאי אהני ליה - ומסתברא למעוטי בן פקועה, דכשחוט דמי, ולא שה הוא; ותפדה מרבי' בעל מום ונקבה ובן שתי שנים, דשה נינהו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 12a:9:1.english: What purpose did “lamb” serve? - And it is reasonable [that it comes] to exclude a ben pekua, since it is considered as [already] slaughtered and is not a [living] lamb; while [from] “you shall redeem,” we include a blemished [animal], a female, and a two-year-old, as they are [indeed] lambs.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 12a:19:1.hebrew: קא משמע לן תחת תחת משלמים גמר - וא"ת: למה לי בבכור "עד שיהא הוא שור ובכורו שור"? נילף "העברה" "העברה" ממעשר! וי"ל: משום דכתיב "אך" לחייב מקצת סימנין דומין לאמו, לכך צריך למעט נדמה בהאי קרא, דנשמע מינה אמאי קאי "אך". ומיהו, לההוא תנא דממעט לעיל נדמה מפטר חמור תרי זמני, וגלי לן בקדושת דמים וה"ה לקדושת הגוף — לפי טעם זה לא הוה מצי למדרש מקצת סימנים מאך; ושמא נפקא ליה מקרא אחרינא:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 12a:19:1.english: "It teaches us: It is derived [from] 'under,' 'under,' from peace offerings" - And if you say: Why do I need [a derivation] regarding a firstborn [to teach]: "until it is an ox and its firstborn is an ox"? Let us derive [it via a verbal analogy of] ha’avarah ha’avarah from [animal] tithe! And one can say: Because it is written "but" [akh] to obligate [an offspring that has] partial characteristics resembling its mother, it is therefore necessary to exclude nedameh in this verse, so that we may learn from it what "but" applies to. However, according to that tanna who excludes nedameh above from [the mention of] a firstborn donkey twice, and it revealed to us [this exclusion] with regard to sanctity of value, and the same applies to bodily sanctity — according to this reasoning, he would not have been able to expound partial characteristics from "but"; and perhaps he derives it from another verse.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 12a:1:1.hebrew: רבי אליעזר מתיר בכלאים - ר' אלעזר גרסינן, ולא גרסינן "רבי אליעזר". וכן מוכח במרובה (ב"ק דף עח.), דאמר: ר' אלעזר דמתיר בכלאים מפני שהוא שה, "דאינו אלא להוציא כלאים" — למאי הלכתא? ומשני: לטמא שנולד מן הטהור ועיבורו מן הטמא. ודלא כר' יהושע — דאי כר' יהושע, מ"שה כבשים ושה עזים" נפקא; וכל שכן דלא כר' אליעזר, דשרי לעיל בפירקין. אלמא דרבי אליעזר פליג על רבי אלעזר, ור' אליעזר בר פלוגתיה דרבי יהושע:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 12a:1:1.english: "Rabbi Eliezer deems it permitted with a hybrid" - We read "R. Eleazar", and we do not read "Rabbi Eliezer". And so is proved in [the chapter entitled] Merubah (Bava Kamma 78a), where it says: According to R. Eleazar, who permits [redemption] with a hybrid because it is a lamb, [as for Rava's principle] that it serves only to exclude a hybrid — for what halakha [is it needed]? And [the Gemara] answers: For an impure [animal] born from a pure [animal] whose conception was from an impure [animal]. And [this explanation is] not in accordance with R. Yehoshua, for if [it were] in accordance with R. Yehoshua, he derives [this] from "a lamb of sheep or a lamb of goats"; and all the more so [it is] not in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, who permits [it] earlier in our chapter. Thus [it is evident] that Rabbi Eliezer disagrees with R. Eleazar, and Rabbi Eliezer is the dispute partner of R. Yehoshua.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 12a:24:1.hebrew: מה צבי ואיל אין פודין וכו' - עוד יש דרשא בפ' שני (לקמן בכורות דף טו.) מצבי ואיל: דפטר להו ממתנות, ואי לאו מיעוטא דקרא — הוה שרי חלבו, ופטר להו מאותו ואת בנו. וא"ת: היכי עבדינן כל הנך דרשות, דפרק כל פסולי (לקמן בכורות דף לג.) אמר: "תלתא צבי ואיל כתיבי", ומייתי כל חד למילתיה, ולא דרשינן מינייהו הך דרשות כלל:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 12a:24:1.english: “Just as one may not redeem [with] a gazelle or a hart, etc.” - There is another derivation in the second chapter (below, Bekhorot 15a) from “gazelle and hart,” that exempts them from [priestly] gifts; and were it not for the exclusion of the verse, it would have permitted their [forbidden] fat and exempted them from [the prohibition of] “it and its offspring.” And if you say: How do we make all these derivations, seeing that the chapter [entitled] “Kol Pesulei” (below, Bekhorot 33a) says: “Three [times] 'gazelle and hart' are written,” and it brings each one for its own matter, and we do not derive these derivations from them at all?!
